Test build. Install into a fresh arm64ec container.

GE-Proton 10.0-34 arm64ec (bionic) from [The412Banner](https://github.com/The412Banner/proton-wine) (`proton_10.34-GE`), plus ntsync with a userspace backend.

Proton 10 has no ntsync of its own, so this build adds two pieces:

- **ntsync client/server support**: Elizabeth Figura's in-process synchronization series as carried for Proton 10 by [CachyOS/wine-cachyos](https://github.com/CachyOS/wine-cachyos) (`cachyos_10.0_20260426/main`).
- **Userspace backend**: [GameNative/ntsync-android](https://github.com/GameNative/ntsync-android), used when the device has no usable `/dev/ntsync` (most Android kernels).

## How the sync backend is chosen

wineserver decides once at startup, and every Wine process follows its choice:

1. `/dev/ntsync`, if it opens and a test object can be created on it.
2. Otherwise userspace ntsync: a shared memory region at `$NTSYNC_SHM`, or `$TMPDIR/ntsync_userspace.*.shm`.
3. If both fail, server-side synchronization.

While ntsync is active, esync and fsync are switched off in wineserver and in every process together, so the esync setting doesn't have to be turned off first. If you want esync instead, set `PROTON_NO_NTSYNC=1`.

## Environment variables

- `PROTON_NO_NTSYNC=1`: disable ntsync (`WINE_DISABLE_FAST_SYNC=1` and `WINENTSYNC=0` do the same)
- `PROTON_NO_KERNEL_NTSYNC=1`: use the userspace backend even when `/dev/ntsync` works
- `NTSYNC_SHM=/path/file.shm`: the shared region path, if processes don't share a `TMPDIR`
- `NTSYNC_SPIN_ITERS`, `NTSYNC_DEBUG=1`: library tuning and diagnostics, see the [ntsync-android README](https://github.com/GameNative/ntsync-android#environment-variables)

wineserver logs which backend it picked, e.g. `ntsync: no usable /dev/ntsync, using userspace ntsync.`

## Files

- `GE-proton-10.0-34-ntsync-arm64ec-sdk28.wcp`: GameNative / Bannerlator / WinNative
- `GE-proton-wine-10.0-34-ntsync-arm64ec-sdk28.wcp.xz`: Winlator CMOD & Ludashi

`versionName` is `10.0-9-arm64ec`, so this installs alongside The412Banner's 10.0-34 build instead of replacing it.

## Testing

The same source was built natively for x86_64 Linux, in a container without `/dev/ntsync`, so the userspace backend was in use:

- Wine's `ntdll` and `kernel32` conformance tests for `sync`, `thread`, `process` and `om` give the same results as server-side synchronization (`PROTON_NO_NTSYNC=1`).
- A focused test (events, semaphores, mutexes, wait-all, `SignalObjectAndWait`, `MsgWaitForMultipleObjects` on thread messages, alertable APC waits, named objects across processes, `WAIT_ABANDONED` after the owning process exits) passes.
- An event ping-pong between two threads takes 34 µs per round trip, against 66 µs with server-side synchronization.

## Known limitations

- Not yet tested on an Android device. If a game misbehaves, compare against `PROTON_NO_NTSYNC=1` first.
- `GE-proton-10.0-34-ntsync-20260924-7` is superseded: in that build wineserver dropped its ntsync device after the first request, so everything silently fell back to server-side synchronization.
- The userspace backend requires wineserver and every Wine process to see the same `TMPDIR` (or `NTSYNC_SHM`). A process that can't attach to the shared region logs an error and falls back to server calls.
